newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields still higher on EMU worries.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields still higher on EMU worries.

text.p: Swedish debt yields were higher and the crown weaker on Monday on rumours which started Friday that Europe's monetary union (EMU) could be delayed by two years, dealers said.
"I think yields could come up even further. If you start talking about delaying the start of EMU it might turn out to be delayed by more than two years -- say, five years or more," one dealer said.
The crown softened to 4.4600 crowns to the mark compared to 4.4340 on Friday on concerns over EMU.
"The crown is following the Italian lira," one dealer said.

Focus was on the U.S. NAPM index expected at 1500 GMT, German unemployment due on Thursday and U.S. payroll data on Friday. The market was awaiting U.S. figures for hints about whether or not interest rates would be raised.
Six month T-bill rate rose five basis points to 4.22 percent and the ten tear bond yield rose nine basis points to 6.88 percent.
